Use case: identity-preserve. Create a corrected six-key blacksmith HAMMERING animation sprite sheet of the EXACT woman in attached approved neutral sprite. This is a biomechanics repair, not a character redesign. SIX COLUMNS, ONE ROW, six complete full-body sprites on transparent background, equal cells, same original low-resolution pixel density and detailed warm pixel-art style. Original head-to-body ratio and side-swept copper ponytail, original face, narrow original eyes, ivory rolled shirt, olive trousers, brown boots. NO apron or gloves yet. Character faces RIGHT THREE-QUARTER. Feet, legs, pelvis, waist belt line and trouser pixels MUST stay in precisely identical places in every cell, both feet planted. The torso must PIVOT about the FIXED PELVIS, with its neck and head moving as one connected body. DO NOT pin head in place. DO NOT slide torso backwards away from head. DO NOT cut torso from hips.
POSES left to right: 0 ready holding hammer in anatomical right/near hand and tongs in far hand; 1 hammer raised above shoulder, upper chest rotates slightly back and head follows naturally; 2 downswing torso inclines forward from fixed hip; 3 contact, torso visibly leans forward to right about15degrees, shoulders move right3px/down3px and head moves right4px/down6px (native units) as part of same connected neck/chest, near hand hammer at waist-level strikepoint, far hand tongs stay at fixed waist-level workpiece; 4 recoil halfway back with upper body and head moving together; 5 ready matches0.
The near shoulder, upper arm, elbow, wrist and hammer must form a continuous limb in every pose. In bent pose, head+neck+shoulders+arms all incline together, continuous shirt from neck through waist, no gaps. Lower body remains the same throughout. Keep hammer shape, hand ownership, fixed workpiece strikepoint and tongs continuous. No furniture, no background, no labels, no additional hands. Render original native appearance about117pixels tall on128x160 cells, simple1px dark outline, no smoothing. Give extra transparent space around raised hammer rather than shrinking person to fit.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Image1 is the six-key correctly connected hammering pose sheet to preserve exactly. Image2 is equipment design only. Keep all six heads, necks, shoulders, torsos, hips, legs, feet and hand positions EXACTLY as image1, including the head and chest leaning forward together in keys2/3/4. Add ONLY the same worn brown leather bib apron/straps/brass buckles/belt/side tools and brown leather work gloves from image2, drawn to FOLLOW each pose's rotated torso, never upright when torso is bent. Apron waist stays attached to fixed pelvis; top follows chest. Gloves enclose the existing hands at their existing grips. Add a small horizontal orange hot steel blank at the tip of tongs, at the same fixed waist-level strike point in all six cells. ALSO remove eyes/eyebrows/mouth lines from all six faces, filling only their interiors with matching skin, so eyes and mouth can be restored as separate exact source layers. Keep nose, blush, complete face shape and all hair unchanged. No other edits. Same six equal columns one row, transparent background, original detailed crisp native pixel-art style and dark1px contour. No furniture.
